key_insight: Atomistic simulations connect alumina inclusion fraction and aluminum grain count to effective elastic properties, strength, and damage behavior in aluminum-matrix nanocomposites.
engineering_relevance: The extracted parameters can inform upper-scale constitutive models for particulate aluminum–alumina nanocomposites.
method: Run molecular statics simulations under tension and compression.
Vary alumina volume fraction in single-inclusion cells and aluminum grain count in polycrystalline representative volume elements.
Extract elastic and failure parameters from stress–strain curves and compare isotropized elastic constants with Voigt–Reuss–Hill estimates.
evidence_signal: Evaluation uses two atomistic model classes, stress–strain responses, and classical elastic estimates, with atomistic outputs informing brittle versus ductile behavior and transgranular versus intergranular fracture.
watch_item: Transferability beyond the simulated atomistic structures requires validation; the abstract reports no experimental comparison or quantitative accuracy metrics.
paper_title: Evaluation of upper-scale mechanical parameters of particulate aluminum-based nanocomposites from molecular simulations
